title: Chapter 51
content:
Il-hyun leaned back, watching with quiet amusement as Jakyeong sketched out the operational map on a scrap of paper.

The drawing detailed Il-hyun's exact standing position on the dais alongside Jakyeong’s sniper nest across the street. The draftsmanship was so atrocious that Il-hyun couldn't help bursting into a laugh, remembering how the kid had initially claimed to be a fine arts major.

Having scouted the venue beforehand, Jakyeong pinpointed the marks with tactical precision.

"Right here. The second you step out from behind the podium to take your bow, I'll take the shot."

On the building opposite, Jakyeong had drawn Il-hyun as a stick figure, though instead of leaving the head blank, he had deliberately given the face a pair of ferociously sharp, villainous eyes. Il-hyun stared down at the doodle with a look of mild offense. They say drawings reflect the subconscious... Is this truly how rotten I look inside his head?

After treating him so lavishly, it stung a little.

In the operational plan, the high-velocity round was supposed to strike Il-hyun dead-center in the left chest.

While Jakyeong walked through the ballistic trajectory, Il-hyun simply sat opposite, leaning on his palm to study the kid's features.

Noticing the lack of focus, Jakyeong tapped the tabletop sharply with the back of his pen. "Pay attention. Are you even listening to me?"

"Go on," Il-hyun murmured.

"A concealed ballistic vest will stop the bullet, but it won't absorb the blunt kinetic trauma," Jakyeong continued, his tone clinical. "Catch a bad break, and you're looking at shattered ribs or internal contusions. Though given your frame, you shouldn't have much to worry about."

"Naturally," Il-hyun said, chin tilting upward as he squared his broad shoulders with a cocky grin. "There isn't a single fragile inch on this body."

Jakyeong pointedly ignored the flex. "Regardless, that's your burden to manage."

Il-hyun remained fixated on Jakyeong’s mouth. I thought only his eyes were exquisite, but those full, delicate lips aren't bad either.

"And you are strictly prohibited from demanding any form of medical compensation from me afterward," Jakyeong added firmly.

Il-hyun let out a low chuckle. "Do I strike you as that petty?"

"Yes."

The instant, unhesitating verdict earned a wounded pout. "How cruel. Want me to show you what truly petty looks like?"

"Spare me. In any case, my contract ends the second the trigger is pulled. The aftermath is entirely on you. If you're genuinely anxious, station a trauma surgical unit on standby in the subterranean bay."

Il-hyun smiled warmly. "I'm not worried. I trust you, darling."

Jakyeong’s dark pupils flickered with a subtle tremor.

Reaching across the mahogany surface, Il-hyun caught Jakyeong’s wrist and pressed the flat of his palm over his left breast pocket. "You're going to put it right here. Cleanly."

Jakyeong shifted the man's fingers an inch inward. The heart is here.

Thump. Thump. Thump.

The slow, steady beat of Il-hyun's heart resonated against Jakyeong's palm. Feeling the rhythmic heat seep into his own skin made Jakyeong pull his hand back, but Il-hyun gripped his fingers tight, dragging them down to press flat over his hardening groin.

"Though it seems my heart beats down here instead."

"..."

"Feel that? Pumping fiercely, isn't it?"

Feeling the thick shaft swell beneath the tailored slacks, Jakyeong snatched his hand back with an expression of pure disgust.

Il-hyun winced in mock pain, then broke into a grin. He reached over, plucking the fountain pen from Jakyeong’s grip. Jakyeong watched as Il-hyun added broad, muscular shoulders to his stick-figure doodle, asking if this looked more true to life.

Jakyeong let out an incredulous scoff. The senior housekeeper hadn't been exaggerating—the man was annoyingly good at everything he touched. With just a few effortless strokes, the doodle looked remarkably stylized.

Then, Il-hyun began sketching Jakyeong's face, exaggerating his large, dark eyes like an extraterrestrial. Beside the sketch, he wrote the three characters of his true name in crisp, calligraphic perfection: Lee Ja-kyeong.

He finished it off by drawing a neat little heart right next to the name.

Jakyeong scowled, snatching the paper back. Despite his annoyance, a faint, unwanted warmth crept up the back of his neck and onto his cheeks.

Twirling the pen between his fingers, Il-hyun rested his chin on his palm, studying the flush. "Look at you... blushing like a schoolboy over a single little heart."

"Does it not occur to you that I might just be creeped out and furious?"

"Not in the slightest," Il-hyun smirked, crooking an index finger. "Come here."

"Why?"

"We won't see each other after tomorrow. I'm collecting my goodbye kiss."

"Not happening."

Before the refusal fully cleared Jakyeong's throat, Il-hyun pushed himself up from his chair, bracing both hands on the table and leaning across.

Jakyeong moved to dodge, but he was a split-second too late.

Large fingers tangled into the hair at the nape of his neck, tilting his chin upward as firm lips sealed over his. The kiss started soft before a hot, slick tongue breached his mouth, sweeping over his palate with possessive heat.

Their breaths tangled, growing ragged. Il-hyun’s free hand slid to Jakyeong’s collar, working the buttons of his dress shirt loose. This time, Jakyeong didn't fight the intrusion.

Knock, knock.

The sudden rap at the door froze them both.

Breaking the kiss, Il-hyun turned an irritated scowl toward the entrance.

"Director Kang, are you inside?"

It was Park Tae-soo.

Letting out a heavy sigh, Il-hyun glanced down at Jakyeong. The kid had his head ducked, the tips of his ears burning a vivid crimson as he hurriedly folded the operational map away. The sheer sight of him acting flustered was so endearing that Il-hyun let out a quiet, helpless chuckle.

A searing, blinding agony tore through his left thigh.

Il-hyun looked down to find dark, arterial crimson geysering from the mangled fabric of his trousers. A split second later, a second high-caliber round shattered his right leg. His knees buckled, and his body slammed backward onto the stage, the back of his skull striking the floor with a hollow crack.

Chaos erupted. Screaming guests stampeded for the exits, and Kang Yu-jung’s pale, terrified face appeared above him, desperately pressing her hands over his bleeding legs while screaming for Park Tae-soo.

His vision blurred at the edges, his breath turning shallow and ragged. The shrieks, sirens, and metallic clatter of automated shutters sounded distant, muffled under water.

Hands hoisted him onto a stretcher. His eyelids grew impossibly heavy, his core temperature plunging into an icy chill as blood drained from his limbs.

Tilting his head to the side, he caught the faces of his family standing nearby: Kim Sun-young, Kang Tae-han, Kang Seok-joo—all frozen in panic.

And then there was Chairman Kang.

The old patriarch stood among the chaos with an utterly serene expression. In fact, the corners of his mouth seemed to be curling into a faint, satisfied smile.

Il-hyun fixed a venomous, blood-soaked glare on the old man, his lips parting into a fractured, mocking grin.

Don't celebrate just yet, old man.

Even if I rot in the deepest pit of hell... I will drag myself back to take you with me.

So wait for me.

He clenched his jaw, darkness steadily swallowing his field of view.

The striking, delicate face of Lee Ja-kyeong flashed through his fading consciousness. Clever little devil... Putting on that pretty, innocent face only to stab me straight in the back.

His eyelids fell shut, plunging his world into absolute silence as his consciousness sank into the pitch-black void.

The concrete safehouse was cluttered with rusted machinery and discarded shipping crates. It was an abandoned parts factory managed by an associate of Wang Ryun—completely locked down from the outside world, making it an ideal extraction hub.

Kang Il-hyun’s enforcers had already locked down every private marina along the coast. An underworld contact had reached out, warning that squads of sharp-suited fixers were sweeping the docks brandishing high-resolution photos of Lee Ja-kyeong.

They needed to lie low for several days until the coastal cordon frayed, then slip aboard a local fishing trawler to rendezvous with an offshore smuggling freighter. Ryun was traveling with Jakyeong to rejoin Wang Han, who had liquidated their safehouses in Bangkok and relocated their operational base to Vladivostok.

Jakyeong tossed back a handful of prescription painkillers with a gulp of water. Beside him, Ryun prepped a curved suture needle and sterile monofilament thread. Ryun had always possessed a freakish dexterity for mechanics and craftsmanship, making him the most skilled field surgeon among them.

Swabbing the lacerated forearm with iodine, Ryun methodically pulled the parted flesh together. Jakyeong clenched his jaw, swallowing every whimper of pain. Cold sweat beaded along his brow, the cords in his neck standing out in sharp relief.

Watching the stoic endurance, Ryun shook his head. "Tough bastard... You don't even flinch, do you?"

["Stop playing hard to get... Let me hear that lovely voice."]

The memory of Kang Il-hyun’s gravelly rasp flashed through his mind without warning. Jakyeong ground his teeth even harder, forcing the specter away. If I hadn't shot his legs, Tae-soo's hit squad would have put a bullet in the back of my skull.

Still, since he had avoided center-mass, the man would survive. Jakyeong knew Il-hyun had a private surgical team on standby regardless of his arrogant boasts.

"Strip your shirt off," Ryun said, setting the needle down. "Let me check for secondary shrapnel."

Jakyeong froze. The violent tapestry of crimson love bites, bruises, and scratches Il-hyun had mapped across his ribs and back was still raw.

Before he could deflect, Ryun hooked the hem of the t-shirt, tugging it up. His eyes nearly popped out of his skull at the sight of the deep purples and reds scattered across his skin.

"Whoa... what the hell is this?"

Jakyeong yanked the fabric down, forcing an awkward cough. "It's nothing."

"I've been on this earth eight years longer than you, kid. You think I don't know what a roll in the sheets looks like?"

"I said it's nothing."

"Look at you! How the hell did you manage to pull a girl in the middle of a high-security hit?"

Jakyeong clamped his mouth shut, staring at the floorboards. It wasn't a woman. If the Wang brothers ever found out that Lee Ja-kyeong had spent his nights getting bent over and taken by a syndicate heir, they would never let him live it down.

"Must've been an absolute wildcat," Ryun chuckled, packing away the medical kit.

When Ryun reached to take another look, Jakyeong scrambled up and walked over to the dust-streaked window.

Watching him stand silently by the glass, Ryun felt an odd, unfamiliar disconnect. Usually, concluding a high-profile contract left Jakyeong looking loose and unburdened. Today, he looked like a man who had left an essential piece of himself behind.

"What's on your mind?" Ryun asked quietly.

Jakyeong gave a faint, bitter smile. "Thinking I should permanently retire from acting."

Ryun nodded in wholehearted agreement. "A remarkably wise decision."

Truth be told, Jakyeong had never imagined his acting skills were quite that atrocious. Wang Han’s warnings before deploying to Seoul hadn't been an exaggeration. Throwing an unpredictable sociopath like Kang Il-hyun into the equation had only made keeping his cover a nightmare.

After a few more minutes of banter, Ryun set up a makeshift cot in the corner and turned in for the night.

Leaving the warehouse floor, Jakyeong stepped out into the enclosed loading dock, lighting a cigarette. Their getaway car was concealed beneath a heavy canvas tarp, the perimeter gates secured with active IR sensors and alarms.

Looking up, the night sky was dense with bruised, heavy storm clouds. More rain on the way.

He took a slow drag, exhaling a plume of gray smoke as he rubbed his aching temples. The heavy dose of analgesics was finally taking effect, dulling the throbbing ache in his sutured arm.

A faint rustling sound in the scrap yard caught his attention.

His hand drifted toward his concealed sidearm—only for a soft mew to break the silence. Twin amber eyes gleamed from the shadows beside an oil drum.

A tiny calico kitten poked its head out, stumbling into the open on wobbly legs.

Just as Jakyeong took a step forward, a sleek black stray stepped into the light, its spine arched and eyes blazing with fierce maternal caution.

Jakyeong halted in his tracks. The mother cat let out a low, warning hiss, baring tiny fangs.

Jakyeong chuckled, taking two slow steps back. Reassured, the mother scooped the kitten by the scruff and vanished into the darkness of the yard.

Crushing his cigarette butt against the concrete, Jakyeong stepped back inside and slid the heavy deadbolt into place.

Ryun’s rhythmic snoring echoed through the rafters. Jakyeong envied the man's uncanny ability to sleep like a rock in any hostile environment.

Collapsing onto a battered sofa, Jakyeong closed his eyes, hoping the painkillers would knock him out for good.

Yet the moment his consciousness began to drift, the wicked, grinning face of his former employer forced its way back into his thoughts, haunting his restless sleep until the first gray light of dawn broke over the skyline.
